questions.q: What does a producer actually send to Kafka?
options: A key-value pair (key optional) plus the target topic name
A SQL INSERT statement
A request that must be acknowledged by every consumer before it completes
A file upload to a broker's local disk
questions.explain: At the surface, the whole mental model is: pick a topic, optionally pick a key, send a value.

questions.q: If two events both use the key "order-4471", where do they land?
options: In the same partition, every time — Kafka hashes the key deterministically
In a random partition each time, with no relationship to each other
Always in partition 0, regardless of the key's value
Split evenly across all partitions to balance load
questions.explain: Kafka hashes the key to pick a partition deterministically, so the same key always lands in the same partition.

questions.q: How does a Kafka consumer actually receive events?
options: It polls — subscribing to a topic and repeatedly asking the broker for anything new in a loop
The broker pushes each event to the consumer the instant it's written
It receives events only once per day in a scheduled batch
It must query a separate database that mirrors the topic
questions.explain: Kafka consumers pull: they call poll() in a loop rather than being pushed to by the broker.

questions.q: Why does a producer's choice to send with no key affect partition assignment?
options: With no key, there's nothing to keep together, so Kafka spreads events across partitions instead
Kafka rejects any produce call that doesn't include a key
Events with no key are dropped and never written
Events with no key are all forced into a single dedicated partition
questions.explain: Without a key, there is no entity to keep ordered together, so the client distributes events across partitions (round-robin or sticky).

questions.q: What does it mean that producers and consumers are decoupled?
options: A producer writes to a topic with no idea who (if anyone) is reading it, and vice versa for a consumer
Producers and consumers must be deployed on the same machine
A producer can only write if at least one consumer is already subscribed
Consumers must know the exact producer that wrote each event
questions.explain: The topic is the only thing connecting them, which is what lets you add another independent consumer later with zero producer changes.
